$comment: State-theme runs that are measured but cannot currently reach the <=3% gate,
each with the reason it is blocked and the row that owns it. This file is a
ratchet, not an excuse list: `gate.mjs` fails on any failure NOT listed here,
and equally on any entry here that has started passing, so the list can only
shrink. Every entry must also appear in the MX-VIS register in

gaps.MX-VIS-036--light: Kit self-contradiction: SubdeckList.jsx renders crumbs + FilterRow + list, the shot draws a DECKS section and no filter chips. Owner rulings 2026-07-25 (JSX is the source of truth) and 2026-07-26 (the shot will not be regenerated) make this a permanent recorded gap, not a parked one. The app follows the JSX; this entry exists so the ratchet still blocks every other regression.
gaps.MX-VIS-037--light: Same kit self-contradiction, loading branch: the shot is a skeleton of chrome the JSX never renders. Permanent per the 2026-07-26 ruling.
gaps.MX-VIS-069--light: Measured: 7.67% light / 9.45% dark (8.35 / 10.43 before the create FAB landed). Every section of the kit composition is built and correct; the residual is four things that cannot be built here. (1) The strip carries 2 of the kit's 4 stats — minutes-studied has no producer at all (`int-9`) and words-learned-today is recorded only when a daily goal exists (`int-12`); the two missing cells shorten the strip by one row and shift everything below it up, which is most of the diff. (2) The app bar's notification bell needs a notifications feature and (3) its avatar an account, both WBS 14.x. Recorded rather than parked: the number is real and the causes are enumerated, so the ratchet blocks any regression while the row stays honest about why it is not green.
gaps.MX-VIS-078--light: Measured: 24.88% light / 25.29% dark. Same kit self-contradiction the owner ruled on for MX-VIS-036/037 (2026-07-25 JSX is the standard; 2026-07-26 the shots will not be regenerated), one screen over. `ReviewMode.jsx` gives a study screen a nested app bar - back arrow, mode title, `format_size` and `more_vert` - with the progress header as the body's first child, which is what this build renders. The `study-session--*` shots draw a different shell: an X, the progress inline in the bar, one overflow. The app follows the JSX. Proved by measurement rather than assumed: seeding the shot's own scenario (25 cards, the 21st, prompting `school`) moved it 24.50 -> 24.88, so the counter and the prompt were never the residual. What is left that is buildable is the two app-bar actions the JSX names, and both are product-undefined (int-5).
gaps.MX-VIS-079--light: Measured: 28.59% light / 28.96% dark. Two causes, both recorded rather than parked. (1) The same shots-versus-JSX contradiction as MX-VIS-078: this build renders the shell `ReviewMode.jsx` describes and the shot draws another. (2) The copy decides the layout here: exit-study-session.md §4 writes `Keep studying` / `Save and exit`, which say that leaving *saves*; the kit's shot writes `Stay` / `Leave`, which do not. The app's pair does not fit the kit's side-by-side halves at 390dp, so it wraps and the dialog grows a row taller than the shot. Clipping them to `Keep s...` / `Save a...` was the alternative and was worse. (2) is an owner ruling: adopt the kit's shorter labels, or keep the spec's and accept the taller dialog.
gaps.MX-VIS-084--light: Measured 2026-07-28 over the kit's own scenario: 4.37% light / 6.57% dark (`int-106`). The first number on this row was 1.95/3.20 over a sparse fixture — one English card where the shot lists three Korean ones — and matching the shot's content made the ratio worse, which is the point: the earlier number measured the content, not the composition. Three causes, all named. (1) The screen draws a labelled `MxTextField` where the kit draws its search dock, so the whole list sits a label's height low; the swap is written and held back because the harness cannot drive the dock (`fillField`'s `toHaveValue` fails against it), and shipping an unmeasurable change to a screen that finally has a row is what `int-105` existed to stop. (2) The kit's rows carry an SRS status badge this build will not draw — its own `Chips.jsx` says "Search does not index Progress content (update-search-index.md §3) — see ADR-009 / CF-14", and §3 reads "Không index Progress/Account/private fields ngoài explicit scope", so the badge needs data the index is forbidden to hold. (3) The chip row is four of the kit's six: Language and Deck scope are unbuilt filter dimensions. (4) The kit dims the whole hidden row; the feature layer may not read the opacity token (`memox.design_system.no_theme_token_imports`), so the dimming needs a shared affordance. Its cost is measured, not guessed: with it the run was 3.93/5.74, so dropping it is worth 0.44 light / 0.83 dark.
gaps.MX-VIS-090--light: Measured 2026-07-28 on first registration: 13.33% light / 18.39% dark (`int-110`). The composition is right and in the kit's order — scope card, five mode rows with their tiles, descriptions and radios, the no-SRS note, the block CTA — and the diff image shows why the number is large anyway: a cumulative vertical drift. Each row sits slightly lower than the shot's, the error accumulates downward, and by the last mode the offset is most of a row, which displaces the note and the CTA entirely. One cause is ruled out by measurement rather than by eye: replacing the hand-placed section gaps with the kit's single list rhythm moved light 14.68 -> 13.33 and dark 18.40 -> 18.39, so the gaps were not it. What remains is the row height itself — `MxCard(padding: sm)` around `MxIconTile` against the kit's `MxCard padding="sm"` — and closing this wants those metrics compared, not another layout guess. A smaller, known contribution: the scope card's second line reads the deck name where the shot reads "By schedule", because the kit's scope sheet is unbuilt and the card states the scope it will actually use.
